Done. The plan passed on its first execution and the output verifies bit-exactly.

**What the plan does** (`out/T2/plan.yaml`): after preflight asserts on the 114-tensor count and the 64 attention projections' input shapes, it rebuilds each of the 64 head-bearing tensors per layer with a three-step triple: concat the two kept slices (rows or columns 0..639 and 768..2047) into a temporary name, delete the original, move the temporary back to the original name. Rows are concatenated on dim 0 for q, k, v and columns on dim 1 for o_proj. The required checks are asserted before writing, plus broader ones for every layer, no leftover temporaries, and exactly 114 tensors.

**Verification** with an independent check of the written file against the input shards:

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Tensor count and key set | 114, identical to input |
| Layer-0 q/k/v shape | [1920, 2048] |
| Layer-0 o_proj shape | [2048, 1920] |
| Bit-exact values vs. expected slices, all 114 tensors | 0 mismatches |

**Executions**: 1, no failures. `out/T2/REPORT.md` is written with the self-report fields. The main pitfall noted there is that concat only accepts single-tensor sources, so the plan needs a per-layer, per-tensor entry rather than a single regex rewrite.
